questions.q: What is the primary heat source Arthur Holmes identified for generating mantle convection currents?
questions.a: Radioactive decay of elements (uranium, thorium, potassium) in the mantle generates the thermal energy that drives convection currents. A wrong answer (e.g., "solar heating" or "core cooling only") reveals the student confuses surface processes with deep Earth heat sources and misses the radiogenic heat concept central to Holmes' model.

questions.q: Explain why Holmes' theory successfully addressed the major criticism of Wegener's Continental Drift Theory.
questions.a: Wegener could not provide a credible driving force (his tidal and polar flight forces were physically insufficient). Holmes supplied a viable mechanism: mantle convection currents driven by radiogenic heat, capable of exerting sufficient drag on continental bases. A wrong answer indicates the student does not grasp the "force problem" as the core weakness of Wegener's hypothesis or how convection solves it.

questions.q: A cross-section shows a rising convection limb beneath a continental mass. Predict the sequence of surface geological events at that location over millions of years.
questions.a: Step 1: Upwelling heats and domes the lithosphere. Step 2: Tensional stresses cause radial fracturing and rift valley formation. Step 3: Continued divergence splits the continent, creating a new ocean basin (e.g., Red Sea stage). Step 4: Passive margins form as seafloor spreading continues. A wrong sequence (e.g., immediate mountain building) shows confusion between rising (divergent) and descending (convergent) limbs.

questions.q: Compare the surface expressions of a rising convection limb versus a descending convection limb in Holmes' model. Relate each to modern plate boundary types.
questions.a: Rising limb: continental doming, rifting, volcanic activity, new ocean basin formation → corresponds to divergent boundaries (mid-ocean ridges, continental rifts). Descending limb: oceanic trench, island arc, fold mountains, deep earthquakes → corresponds to convergent boundaries (subduction zones). A wrong comparison (e.g., associating trenches with rising limbs) reveals failure to link vertical mantle flow to horizontal plate motions.

questions.q: Evaluate the statement: "Holmes' convection current theory was widely accepted immediately because it perfectly explained all continental movements."
questions.a: False. The theory was initially ignored because: (1) no direct evidence of mantle convection existed; (2) mantle was thought too rigid for convection; (3) ocean floor data was lacking. Acceptance came only after 1950s-60s paleomagnetic and seafloor spreading evidence. A student agreeing with the statement shows ignorance of the historical scientific resistance and the evidentiary gap that persisted for decades.

questions.q: Design a labeled diagram showing a complete convection cell in Holmes' model, including: heat source, rising limb, lateral flow direction, descending limb, and resulting surface features at both ends. Annotate with forces acting on the continental block.
questions.a: A complete diagram must show: (1) Radioactive heat source in lower mantle; (2) Rising hot plume under continent causing doming/rifting (tensional force → divergent boundary); (3) Horizontal flow dragging continent laterally (shear force); (4) Descending cold limb at oceanic margin forming trench/island arc (compressional force → convergent boundary); (5) Return flow at depth. Missing any component (especially force annotations) indicates incomplete mental model of the theory's mechanical linkage.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Arthur Holmes' ______ Current Theory (1928-1930) proposes that thermal convection currents generated by radioactive decay in Earth's mantle provide the mechanical force driving continental drift, with rising limbs under continents causing divergence and descending limbs at margins causing convergence.
Fill in the blank: Begin by recalling Wegener's inability to explain *what force* moves ______ (tidal force and polar flight force were rejected).
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: Student can explain the mechanism of mantle convection currents as a driving force for continental movement, differentiate between rising and descending limbs and their surface expressions, and articulate why this theory resolved the "force problem" in Wegener's hypothesis.
